reality_delta: The review request describes a real broken loop and a plausible fuse design, but the evidence supplied is only pointers to source files and an events log. No actual diff, no new test assertions, and no host-contract change are shown. The three 'changed_reality' bullets are observations of current behavior, not proof that the intended fix has landed or been validated.
main_concern: The design risks swapping a visible infinite-blocking loop for an invisible deferred-problem loop. The prompt asserts that Stop should switch to 'continue' after max rounds and record audit evidence, but it does not show that the host adapter will honor continue=true for a Stop payload, or that the audit marker cannot be mistaken for 'issue resolved.'
top_risks: Host re-feed logic may key only on decision=block and ignore decision=continue, so the loop continues even after the fuse trips.
An audit field named 'max-correction-rounds' without an explicit 'released_not_resolved' flag may be read by later tooling as 'problem handled,' creating false confidence.
If the correction counter is per-turn, the same underlying issue can re-trigger the same fuse on every subsequent turn, producing a slower but equally broken loop.
missing_evidence: Proposed code diff for build_advisory_stop_payload and print_advisory_stop showing the exact decision/audit fields emitted when current_round > max_rounds.
Host-side contract or test showing that continue=true from Stop halts re-feeding for the current (session_id, turn_id).
End-to-end regression test that verifies exactly one blocking suggestion, one explicit-override path, and one max-round fuse release with no further Stop invocations for the same turn.
minimum_fix: Change the Stop output to decision=continue only when current_round > max_rounds, and add an unambiguous structured field such as {'fuse_triggered': true, 'resolution_status': 'released_not_resolved'}. Add a regression test asserting the full sequence (block → block → continue-with-fuse-marker → no further Stop calls). Document that the host must treat continue=true from Stop as terminal for that turn.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Tie the correction counter to (session_id, turn_id, constraint_key) and include a hash or excerpt of the repeated suggestion in the fuse audit record, so the release proves the loop was recognized rather than merely reaching a numeric threshold.

user_intent_alignment: Good. The user wants Norven's answer to conclude without disabling Stop, without losing the first-two-round advisory behavior, and without silent passing of real issues. The proposal matches this intent. Drift would occur only if the release were implemented as unconditional silence instead of an audited, clearly-marked fuse release.
